title: Compatibility adapter and migration playbook for embeddings + rerank clients
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Multiple internal and external clients are relying on legacy embeddings/rerank endpoint semantics (Link headers, legacy cursor tokens, heterogeneous error codes, and slightly different structured score fields). The new unified embeddings+rerank API provides a cleaner contract but breaks some clients. This ticket scopes a compatibility adapter and a stepwise migration playbook. Goals: (1) Provide a lightweight runtime adapter that translates legacy clients' requests and responses to the new API without duplicating expensive compute, (2) Normalize HTTP and application error semantics across legacy and new clients, (3) Offer a predictable deprecation and opt-in strict mode path for customers to migrate, (4) Ensure parity for pagination behaviors (cursor lifecycle, Link header, page_size semantics) and structured outputs (score fields, metadata and streaming behaviour) while preserving throughput and latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter can accept legacy Link header pagination and return a next_cursor in the unified response with equivalent result set ordering
Requests with legacy cursor tokens are translated to the canonical cursor format; adapter validates and rejects malformed legacy cursors with 400 + stable error.code

Error mapping table implemented so client-visible HTTP status and JSON error.code match documented parity matrix (see technical_decision link), with automated tests covering transient vs permanent errors
Adapter supports both single-shot and streaming rerank responses; streaming clients that expect chunked results receive identical score fields and message boundaries
Compatibility mode is behind an opt-in header X-RW-Compat: legacy-embed-rerank; default behavior is the new unified contract
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with metrics dashboards tracking latency, error-rate, token-cost delta, and model output diffs
Migration playbook documented in Confluence with migration steps, sample client patch snippets, and rollback instructions
technical_decision: Canonical error model: all adapter-translated responses include an application-level 'error.code' string and 'error.message' plus an HTTP status. Mapping rules: legacy 400/422 -> 400 (error.code: 'invalid_request'), legacy 429 -> 429 ('rate_limit'), 5xx -> 502 ('upstream_unavailable') for transient, 500 with 'model_failure' preserved when model returns structured error.

Pagination parity: adapter will support legacy Link header style and expose canonical 'next_cursor' in JSON. Internal implementation maps legacy cursor to canonical cursor (opaque token) and stores minimal cursor metadata in the cache layer; cursor tokens are HMAC-signed to prevent tampering.

Structured outputs: preserve numeric score naming used by legacy clients (e.g., 'score' vs 'scoring.value') by emitting both fields in compatibility mode for one release cycle, with deprecation header advising clients to switch to canonical field 'score_value'.

Streaming: when streaming rerank results, adapter maintains identical chunk boundary semantics and sends a final 'done' structured event. Streaming uses the same socket and chunk format as current streaming API to avoid client parser changes.

Opt-in strictness: add header X-RW-Compat-Mode: strict to enforce canonical behavior and return compatibility warnings when strictness mismatches are detected. Default remains permissive when X-RW-Compat is present without strict.

No model re-evaluation: adapter must not re-run model inference. It only rewrites request/response envelopes and performs superficial sorting/selection compatible with model outputs to maintain cost parity.
implementation_notes: ENG: implement adapter middleware as a thin proxy in the request path with feature flagging via rollout-service
ENG: storage: small ephemeral cursor map in Redis with 7 day TTL and HMAC signing; avoid long-lived persistence to keep token invalidation simple
ENG: add unit/integration tests that replay real traffic patterns from the embed-rerank playback harness (link in related_links)
ENG: add adapter metrics (compat.requests, compat.errors_by_type, compat.latency_p50/95/99, compat.token_cost_delta) to the Console dashboards
QA: create regression prompts and evals comparing outputs between legacy path, adapter path, and canonical API (tolerances defined in migration doc)
SDK: publish small client migration snippet for Node/Python showing header toggle and cursor translation helper
Docs: Confluence + public API docs updates, include deprecation timeline and sample Link header behavior
